title: Announcement and Delivery records, indexes, announces and supersedes relations
description:
Cloud only, no sender wired. Add the Announcement table (id, dedupeKey created with a condition, kind, announces links to Stories with the version looked at, releaseAt in UTC, approval none/soft/hard, approvedBy/At, state planned/released/cancelled/withdrawn, createdBy, trigger, append-only history) and the Delivery table (announcement, channel, account, audience, mode automatic/manual, text and image as S3 keys plus content hash, draftedBy, checks with guideline id/version/hash, state, blockedReason, resultUrl, providerId, cost, counts, attempts, supersedes/supersededBy). Add the announces and supersedes relation types. Reads by index only: by dedupeKey, an Announcement's Deliveries, an account's Deliveries newest first, planned Announcements by releaseAt, a Story's Announcements through the relation. No subscriptions; short fields only, no text in the catalog.

**Acceptance criteria**
- Gherkin: An announcement is decided once (same Story published twice makes one Announcement; a crash between the key and the first Delivery finishes on retry; a publish that qualifies on no channel leaves no row).
- Gherkin: Approval and release (none releases at once, hard gate waits, newer Story version after approval returns to waiting, cancel before release, past releaseAt releases now).
- Gherkin: No text in the catalog (a Delivery row holds no post text, HTML or Markus).
- One live Delivery per Announcement, channel and account; a second needs supersedes, set in one transaction that marks the old one superseded.
- No table scans; every read in the list above is an indexed query.

Design: ~/Projects/papyrus-announcement-delivery-design.md. X feed stays OFF. No real email addresses in specs or fixtures. Every behaviour change ships with narrative Gherkin specs.

**Section 13 additions (2026-11-16, always-on agent review; changes E, H, J)**
Fields and behaviour:
- Approval lives on the Delivery, not the Announcement (change J; corrects design section 2). Each Delivery carries `approval`, `approvalPolicy` (where the value came from), `approvedVersion`, `approvedBy`, `approvedAt`. The Announcement keeps only the decision and `releaseAt`. An approval names one version; a later version is not approved.
- Every wait is a named time on the Delivery (change E): `lockAt` (explicit, filled from the per-kind and per-channel setting at creation; equal to `releaseAt` when there is no separate lock), `nextAttemptAt` with `waitingFor` (`rate limit`, `budget cycle`, `release`), and one sparse `dueAt` that is the earliest of them, with one sparse index on `dueAt`. Also `lockedAt` and `lockedVersion` (a lock is a fact, not something held; change K).
- Attempt outcomes include an open `started` state and `unknown` (change H; behaviour in PPY-a570e8).
**Acceptance criteria (added)**
- Gherkin: a Delivery records approval, approvalPolicy, approvedVersion, approvedBy, approvedAt; a later version than approvedVersion is not approved; two Deliveries of one Announcement can hold different approval values.
- Gherkin: dueAt is the earliest of lockAt, nextAttemptAt and releaseAt; the sparse dueAt index returns due Deliveries and omits Deliveries with no pending time.
- The Announcement record holds no approval fields.

**Always-on agent standard (2026-11-16; design `docs/design/always-on-agents-architecture.md`)**
Built in PR #1618. The decision model is named `AnnouncementDecision` (the deployed model `Announcement` is the old X row shape, deleted by PPY-efd06c); keep that model name. Both models are in an optional model group that a brand-new site's first deploy defers, because the first stage stood at 2,062 resources against a budget of 2,000 (now 1,972); see PPY-e06835. Outcome words on attempts follow PPY-f58445. Findings from reading the branch (corrections, soft-review silence, a row before its file) are recorded on PPY-3e0a8a, PPY-a570e8 and PPY-e8ec54 and checked by PPY-9922b2.
